target_customer: Developers and companies building AI agents that need facts about physical locations, such as land and site selection teams
problem: Facts about places are scattered across GIS, utility, census and county sources built for humans, so agents cannot reliably use them.
business_model: Usage-based API and subscription (per parcel and per page pricing, paid plans from $49 a month)
product_category: Geospatial data API and MCP for AI agents

founders.name: Ansh Chokshi
education: University of Toronto, Computer Science, Math and Economics (per YC page)
previous_startups: Poker Pit (co-founded at 21; reached $250K ARR in four months before an acquisition, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Only founder listed on the YC page. A RuntimeWire article names Shashwat Kapoor as a co-builder; not listed by YC, so not recorded as co-founder.

competitors.name: Regrid
competitors.what: Parcel data API with an MCP server for AI tools

competitors.name: Precisely
competitors.what: Location intelligence with an MCP server for agents

competitors.name: xMap
competitors.what: Data infrastructure for agents covering POI, mobility, parcel ownership

technical_complexity.rationale: Indexing and normalizing about 97 mostly federal sources with citations is solid data engineering; hard parts are coverage and freshness.

defensibility.rationale: Mostly public data and established parcel vendors already offer MCP access.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents had already shipped MCP servers by the time of the batch; no acquisition recorded.

market_need_then: Agents acting in the real world need cited location facts; first customers reportedly used it to source off-market land for data centers, a company claim.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical: physical world context for AI agents

branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN thread and small press mentions; no merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Name resembles a given name and is easy to misspell; little press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Mireye is a Summer 2026 company with a live API, a Launch HN thread and a first-time repeat founder who sold an earlier startup. No funding is public, and parcel data vendors already ship MCP servers, so traction from agent builders will decide the outcome.
notes: One RuntimeWire snippet mentions an acquirer not identified in public materials; this is unclear and not recorded as an exit. Competitor sources are undated. Founding year not stated in sources opened.
